events.title: WSO2 and Adobe Commerce Flaws Exploited in Attacks, Added to CISA KEV
events.summary: A critical path traversal flaw in WSO2 API Control Plane (CVE-2026-5430) has been actively exploited and added to CISA's KEV catalog.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 10.0 and has been added to CISA's KEV catalog after evidence of active exploitation. Defenders should prioritize patching WSO2 API Control Plane to mitigate the path traversal flaw.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-5430 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-09-24, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-09-27.
CVE-2026-5430 is rated 10.0 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-5430 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%.

timeline.summary: First reported by CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
Also reported by The Hacker News

events.title: CVE-2026-71362: Adobe Commerce and Magento Adobe Commerce and Magento Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
events.summary: Adobe Commerce and Magento have a critical incorrect authorization flaw that could let attackers gain elevated access to sensitive resources without user interaction.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 9.1 and is listed on the KEV, indicating it is actively exploited. Its high EPSs score suggests a high likelihood of exploitation in the wild.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-71362 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-09-24, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-09-27.
CVE-2026-71362 is rated 9.1 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-71362 being exploited in the next 30 days at 88%.

events.title: Botslab G980H Dashcams
events.summary: Botslab G980H dashcams are vulnerable to several critical flaws that could let attackers bypass authentication, gain privileged access, alter settings, and disrupt device operation.
events.why_it_matters: The flaws carry high CVSS scores, including 9.2, and are classified as critical, enabling attackers to take full control of the devices and potentially expose sensitive data. Multiple CVEs affect the same firmware version, increasing the attack surface.

claims.text: CVE-2026-81630 is rated 9.2 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it, the highest of the 14 scored CVEs here.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-82566 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%, the highest of the 14 CVEs here.

timeline.summary: First reported by CISA ICS Advisories

events.title: Eufy Omni C20, Omni X10 Pro
events.summary: Eufy Omni C20 and X10 Pro devices with firmware versions below 1.6.4 are vulnerable to OS command injection, hard-coded credentials, and certificate validation flaws that could let attackers run arbitrary code. Three CVEs (CVE-2026-93289, CVE-2026-93290, CVE-2026-93291) are responsible.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerabilities have a CVSS score of 9.4 and are rated critical, meaning attackers could execute arbitrary code on affected devices. These devices are used in critical infrastructure sectors, so a successful exploit could impact essential services.

claims.text: CVE-2026-93291 is rated 9.3 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it, the highest of the 3 scored CVEs here.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-93289 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%, the highest of the 3 CVEs here.

events.title: Can you trust AI with critical infrastructure?
events.summary: In traditional IT, isolating a compromised endpoint can stop an attack. In operational technology (OT) environments, that same action could disrupt control of a pipeline, cause a rupture, or trigger environmental damage. That’s why adopting AI in critical infrastructure requires a fundamentally different security approach. Drawing on more than 25 years of experience across energy, pipelines, aerospace, and defense, Jason Cradit, CTO and CISO at Everline, explains how security leaders can move beyond blanket restrictions and establish practical AI governance and guardrails.
